newsitem.title: USA: International Paper sees better Q2.
newsitem.headline: International Paper sees better Q2.

text.p: International Paper Co said Tuesday that it believes it has reached the bottom of an "extremely difficult" business cycle, and is optimistic that the second quarter will be stronger than the first.

In the first it earned $0.11 per share, compared with $0.36 per share in the year-earlier period. The company added that in current conditions it needs to focus on those business factors that it can control.
It said it has brought its 1997 capital spending target down to $1.2 billion, below its expected level of depreciation, and is not planning to add new capacity in its U.S. pulp and paper businesses.
The company said that industry inventories remained high throughout the quarter, causing prices to decline and hurt earnings.
The company also said it has taken downtime to balance its production with demand, principally in uncoated papers, pulp and containerboard.

The company did add, however, that demand for uncoated grades, particularly copy and printing papers, strengthened in recent weeks in the United States, and April and May price increases of $100 a ton were announced for uncoated grades.
